Business domain map

What Bunkai is for, how it earns, and what every domain term means. Reverse-engineered from upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging commit 98ee1b4 (sections updated 2026-10-13); sections still dated 2026-10-02 were built at main commit e88512e. Every path below is relative to that repository; db:<table> is a table in supabase/migrations/; route:<path> is a page or API route of the app.

Overview

Confidence: Medium. What the product does is verified in code at origin/staging 4ccd8ede (migrations up to 0133, the /api/v1 handlers and the shipped screens). The problem framing and the personas still come from marketing-toned in-repo docs, which keeps the synthesis at Medium.

Problem statement

Bunkai is a Test Management System (TMS). Its metadata reads "Open-core Test Management System. ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases), modular tests, full traceability" (app/layout.tsx). The product docs frame the problem as existing TMSs (Xray, Zephyr Scale, TestRail, qTest) acting as document vaults: duplicated steps across test cases, missing traceability from user story to test to bug, and pass-rate reports that do not say what is validated (.context/business/business-model.md, .context/PRD/executive-summary.md; marketing-toned prose, so confidence is downgraded).

The answer the code enforces is structural. An ATC cannot be created or updated without a user story and at least one of that story's acceptance criteria (the create and update database functions reject an empty or foreign criteria list, supabase/migrations/0021_atc_create_update.sql). Tests chain ATCs by reference, a Run freezes a copy of what it executed, and a bug keeps links to the run step and ATC it came from. That chain (criterion, ATC, Test, Run, Bug) is what the traceability and coverage reports read, and archiving never breaks it: archived work leaves the reuse lists but stays as evidence.

Target users

  • QA engineers and QA leads working inside a workspace, with the roles the database enforces: viewer, member, admin, owner (supabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql), ranked as a ladder for member management (supabase/migrations/0114_workspace_member_removal.sql).
  • Programmatic operators (CLI, CI, AI agents) that authenticate with a Personal Access Token, start Runs as an agent or ci executor and stream step results, or submit an already finished automated Run in one call (supabase/migrations/0121_automated_run_submission.sql, supabase/migrations/0122_streamed_run_step_results.sql).
  • Workspace owners who buy and keep the paid tier (Billing Plan, invoices, failed-renewal recovery) and own data export and deletion.
  • Named personas in the docs (senior QA engineer, QA lead, developer, autonomous AI test agent) remain intent only (.context/PRD/executive-summary.md).

Value proposition (delivered at 4ccd8ede)

  • Multi-tenant workspaces with roles, invite links, member removal along the role ladder, self-service leave, owner deletion with a 30-day restore window that closes on time, and a full data export (route:/settings/workspaces, route:/settings/data-export).
  • An authoring tree: projects, modules (create, rename, move, archive, restore), user stories with a Ready-to-test gate whose archive takes their criteria and ATCs, ordered acceptance criteria, and a one-way Jira story import through each workspace's own Jira connection (components/layout/Sidebar.tsx, route:/settings/jira).
  • An ATC library, per project and workspace-wide (route:/atcs): create, edit, duplicate, search, export, classify, bulk-edit, archive and restore, with mandatory anchoring (components/atcs/).
  • Tests as ordered chains of ATC references with suite tags, listed per project; Test Plans with live progress and a close / reopen verdict; Milestones with attached plans, pooled readiness, an overdue badge and archive (components/tests/, components/test-plans/, components/milestones/).
  • Execution: Runs of a Test against a project environment by a human, an agent or CI, with per-step verdicts, notes, evidence links and screenshot attachments, live updates, automatic close of abandoned runs, one-call submission of automated runs, a comparison with the previous run and a per-Test flakiness signal (components/runs/).
  • Native bug tracking: severity, assignee, a forward-only status lifecycle, content correction, screenshot evidence, filed straight from a failed step; a workspace-wide defect index; a configurable (not yet sending) Jira defect sync (components/bugs/).
  • Quality reports: coverage per criterion and module (and per workspace in one call), a story traceability chain, recovery cycles, a live defect heatmap, a run report split by execution mode, a workspace Test Runs index, Home widgets, a command palette and personal saved views (route:/projects/[projectSlug]/metrics, route:/runs).
  • Team chat per workspace with mentions and rich links to ATCs, Tests and Runs; a notification inbox and a daily email digest whose In-app and Email switches now both apply (components/chat/, components/notifications/).
  • A versioned REST API with OpenAPI docs, scoped tokens and idempotency keys for non-browser callers (app/api/v1/, route:/api/docs).
  • Self-service upgrade from Community to Cloud through Stripe Checkout, plus billing details, card replacement, invoice history and a 14-day grace period on a failed renewal (route:/settings/billing).

Main navigation: Home, Activity, Projects, ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Settings (components/layout/AppSidebar.tsx), plus a "Team chat" button and the notifications bell. ATC Library (/atcs), Test Runs (/runs) and Bug Reports (/bugs) now open workspace-wide indexes; Metrics links into the current project, else the first one (lib/navigation/shell-nav.ts). Inside a project: All ATCs, Tests, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Traceability, Milestones, Test Plans, Settings (app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/project-sub-nav.tsx).

Still not delivered, though the product glossary or docs describe them: per-project chat channels; a writer for a Test's Automation status; a CI results file upload (automated results arrive as JSON through the API); sending bugs to Jira (only the configuration and the queue exist); downgrade, cancellation and an Enterprise path (see discovery gaps).

QA relevance

Business aspectTesting implication
Traceability is the core promiseAnchoring rules (story + at least one of its criteria) and the chain to Test, Run and Bug are the highest-value acceptance checks; a write that bypasses them breaks the product's reason to exist. Archive and restore must keep the evidence reads intact.
Multi-tenant workspacesCross-tenant leakage is the top business risk: negative tests per role and per workspace, including soft-deleted workspaces, private evidence files, chat references into unreadable projects and per-workspace Jira credentials.
API-first for agents and CIToken scopes, expiry, revocation, workspace binding, the executor mode a token may declare, submission validation and step re-report conflicts are business features: test them as such.
Self-service onboardingEmail-first sign-up, OAuth, magic link, first-workspace creation and invite acceptance are the activation funnel: smoke scope.
Coverage drives decisions"Uncovered" and "not run" must never merge; a skipped or blocked latest result counts as not run; archived ATCs count only for what they already ran.
Paid tier and limitsOnly the project limit blocks, and it follows the effective plan (Community after an ended grace period). Checkout and recovery must change the plan only on a confirmed Stripe event.
Irreversible data actionsWorkspace deletion becomes permanent after 30 days and restore is refused past the deadline; member removal revokes tokens and unassigns bugs; queued Jira defects cannot be withdrawn; export expiry and owner-only gates are high-consequence checks.

Workspace

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
WorkspaceWorkspace, workspace_id, bunkai_bootstrap_workspace"Workspace" (Create workspace, workspace switcher, Settings > Workspaces)workspacessupabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql, lib/types.ts, components/settings/WorkspacesList.tsx

Business meaning: the tenant and the billing unit. A team's private space; every project, Test, run, bug, notification and chat message belongs to exactly one workspace, and a person sees only the live workspaces they are an active member of. It has a globally unique URL slug, a name, one or more owners, a Billing Plan tier and, once paid, a purchased seat count, billing details and invoices. Each workspace also owns its #general Team chat channel (created automatically) and, optionally, one Jira connection. A workspace scheduled for deletion is treated by every access check as if it did not exist; an account whose only workspaces are deleted is sent to onboarding.

UI labels: onboarding form with name (placeholder "Acme QA") and slug (placeholder "acme-qa"), button "Create workspace", toast "Workspace created"; switcher toast "Workspace switched."; Settings > Workspaces list with "Leave" and "Delete" actions, the member count linking to the members screen for admins and owners, and toast "<name> was deleted." The active workspace is remembered in a cookie separate from the session (lib/api/workspace-cookie.ts).

Related terms: Workspace member, Workspace invite, Project, Billing Plan, Workspace export, Workspace deletion, Team chat, Jira connection.

Abbreviations: ws (code helpers, e.g. bunkai_is_workspace_member(ws_id)).

Workspace member

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Workspace member (seat)WorkspaceMember, MemberRole, MemberStatus, bunkai_leave_workspace, bunkai_remove_workspace_member, bunkai_workspace_role_rank"Members", "Role", "Remove", "Leave workspace"workspace_memberssupabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql, supabase/migrations/0114_workspace_member_removal.sql, lib/workspaces/member-ladder.ts

Business meaning: a person's seat in a workspace, carrying their role (what they may do) and status (whether the seat is live). Only an active membership grants visibility; write access needs at least the member role; member management needs admin or owner. Roles form a ladder (viewer < member < admin < owner): an admin or owner can remove a teammate whose role does not outrank theirs, so an admin cannot remove an owner, and nobody removes themselves (that is Leave). Removing a teammate unassigns their bugs, revokes their tokens bound to that workspace and the pending invites sent to their email, and is logged as member.removed. A workspace may have several owners. A member can leave on their own, except as the last owner or when they would keep no membership in another live workspace (deleted workspaces do not count); leaving revokes their tokens bound to that workspace. Every membership change goes through these guarded operations; no screen or API writes the seat directly.

UI labels: members page with "Email" and "Role" fields, empty state "No members yet.", per-row "Remove" opening "Remove <email>" ("This removal is not allowed.", "This teammate is no longer a member of this workspace.", "Could not remove <email>. Nothing was changed. Try again."); Settings > Workspaces "Leave" opening the "Leave workspace" dialog.

Related terms: Workspace, Workspace invite, Billing Plan (a seat is counted against the tier), Personal access token, Bug. Values: member role, member status.

Structure: business-data-context sections entity-workspace and flow-invite-and-membership.

Workspace invite

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Invite (invite link)workspace_invites, workspace_invite_secrets, bunkai_accept_workspace_invite"Generate invite link", "Invite revoked.", "Joining workspace…"workspace_invites (+ secret hash in workspace_invite_secrets)supabase/migrations/0010_workspace_invites.sql, supabase/migrations/0118_member_write_paths_locked.sql, app/api/v1/invites/accept/route.ts

Business meaning: an admin's offer for one email address to join a workspace with a given role (never owner). Bunkai sends no invite email: the admin copies the link and shares it. The link expires after 7 days and can be revoked or rotated (a new link replaces the old); who issued it, the address and the role cannot be edited afterwards. An email that already belongs to an active member cannot be invited. Accepting requires being signed in with that same email; it adds the membership or promotes a lower role in one step, and is refused when the person already holds an equal or higher role, or when the inviter is no longer an active admin or owner ranked at least as high as the offered role. Removing a member revokes the pending invites addressed to them.

UI labels: "Generate invite link", placeholder "teammate@company.com", "No invites yet.", toasts "Invite revoked.", "New invite link copied to clipboard."; accept page "Checking session…", "Joining workspace…", "Welcome — you have joined the workspace."; refusal "This invite was sent to a different email address."

Related terms: Workspace, Workspace member, Workspace deletion (revokes pending invites).

Abbreviations: none; say "invite link" or "invite token", never bare "token" (the product glossary reserves it).

Module

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
ModuleModule, ModuleTreeNode, parent_module_id, path, archived_at, archive_batch_id, bunkai_restore_module_subtree"Module", "New module", "New sub-module", folders in "Explorer", "Restore module"modulessupabase/migrations/0002_projects_modules.sql, supabase/migrations/0014_module_soft_delete.sql, supabase/migrations/0117_module_restore.sql, lib/tree.ts

Business meaning: a functional area of the project (a feature or component), nestable into sub-modules up to six levels deep, identified by a slash path (for example auth/login), with an optional description of up to 500 characters. It is where user stories and ATCs live and the unit coverage and the defect heatmap aggregate by, which is why the product treats it as a first-class node, not a folder name. Modules can be renamed and moved (a rename or description change is logged only when the value really changed); "deleting" a module archives it with its whole subtree (sub-modules, stories, criteria, ATCs), while runs and bugs stay readable. An archived module can be restored: the restore brings back exactly the rows that archive took, and leaves items archived separately where they are.

UI labels: "Explorer" sidebar folders; context menu "New sub-module", "New user story", "Rename", "Move", "Delete"; buttons "New module", "Create your first module"; description placeholder "What this module covers."; "Delete module" dialog; "Show archived rows" / "Hide archived rows", "Restore module" dialog; toasts "Archived “<name>”", "Moved “<name>”", "Restored “<name>” with …", "Nothing in this project is archived."; "Module" column in the ATC table; "Select a module…" when filing a bug.

Related terms: Project, User story, ATC, Archive and restore, Coverage, Defect heatmap.

User story

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
User storyUserStory, UserStoryStatus, user_story_id, external_id, external_url, bunkai_archive_user_story"User story", "New user story", "Linked user story", "Draft" / "Ready to test"user_storiessupabase/migrations/0003_authoring.sql, supabase/migrations/0017_acceptance_criteria_ordering.sql, supabase/migrations/0111_user_story_archive_cascade.sql, lib/types.ts

Business meaning: the requirement an ATC proves. It belongs to a module and may point to the same story in an external tracker (a Jira key, unique per project among active stories, and a URL); stories can be typed in or imported from Jira. It carries a Ready-to-test gate: "Ready to test" is the explicit signal that its criteria are settled, needs at least one active criterion, and falls back to "Draft" when the last criterion is removed. The gate is a two-state signal, not a workflow, and blocks nothing else. A story with ATCs cannot be hard-deleted; removing it archives it together with its live criteria and ATCs, in one step with one timestamp, so none of its ATCs stays reachable on its own. There is no story-level restore; a story comes back only when its archived Module is restored.

UI labels: Explorer menu "New user story", "Edit", "Manage criteria", "Remove", "Copy ID"; form placeholders "Refund a paid order", "BK-42" (Jira key), "Describe the story in Markdown."; note "The Jira link is set and cannot be changed."; gate badge "Draft" / "Ready to test", actions "Mark ready to test" / "Back to draft", toasts "Marked ready to test", "Story moved back to draft — it has no criteria left."; ATC editor panel "Linked user story" with search placeholder "Search US- or paste a Jira ID…".

ATC

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
ATC (Acceptance Test Case)Atc, AtcLayer, AtcTechnique, AtcPriority, bunkai_create_atc, bunkai_update_atc, bunkai_bulk_edit_atcs, bunkai_archive_atc"ATC", "All ATCs", "ATC Library", "New ATC", "ATC created", "ATC saved", "Bulk edit ATCs", "Archive ATC"atcssupabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql, supabase/migrations/0021_atc_create_update.sql, supabase/migrations/0124_atc_bulk_edit.sql, components/atcs/AtcEditor.tsx

Business meaning: the product's central unit of authorship: one small, reusable verification of a single observable behaviour, written as ordered steps plus assertions, placed in a module, tagged (at most 10 tags), classified by test layer and optionally by test-design technique and ATC Priority, and anchored to a user story and its criteria. Every save bumps its version and is refused when someone else saved first. Tests reference ATCs instead of copying them, so one edit updates every Test that chains it ("one edit, many tests"). An ATC can be duplicated, searched and exported, browsed across every project in the workspace ATC Library, and bulk-edited: up to 200 selected ATCs at once, one field per change (add or remove tags, move to a Module inside each ATC's story subtree, set layer, set priority), each ATC changed, unchanged or refused on its own with a stated reason, never rolled back as a group. It has no delete: it can be archived on its own (and restored from the archived view) or with its story or module; an archived ATC is read-only and leaves the reuse lists, but stays in the Tests that chain it and in their evidence.

Execution status: the atcs.status column (pass / fail / blocked / skipped / running / unrun) is still shown as a status dot, but no code path writes it, so every ATC reads unrun. Real results live on the run step; coverage, traceability and chat rich links read those.

UI labels: editor fields "Title" (required, at least 3 characters, placeholder "A single observable behaviour — start with a verb"), "Module", "Layer", "Technique", "Priority" ("Not specified" when unset), "Steps", "Assertions", "Tags", "Linked user story", panel state "Anchored"; toasts "ATC created", "ATC duplicated", "ATC saved — N Tests updated"; "Used by" (the Tests that chain it); table filters "All techniques", "All priorities"; "ATC library exported"; empty state "No Acceptance Test Case has been written for this project yet."; bulk bar "Bulk edit the selected ATCs" with "Add tags", "Remove tags", "Move to Module", "Set layer to", "Set priority to", "Review change", dialog "Bulk edit ATCs" ("Changed N ATCs.", "The changes that succeeded were kept. Nothing was rolled back."); "Archive ATC", "This ATC is archived. It is read-only until it is restored."

The product glossary bans "Atomic Test Component" (.context/business/domain-glossary.md §0, §4). Anchoring

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Anchoring (ATC to criteria binding)AtcAcceptanceCriterion, isAnchored, p_ac_ids, error ac_outside_user_story"Anchored" (anchoring panel)atc_acceptance_criteria (many-to-many) + atcs.user_story_idsupabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql, supabase/migrations/0021_atc_create_update.sql, components/atcs/AnchoringPanel.tsx

Business meaning: the traceability rule that defines the product: an ATC is anchored when it names one user story and at least one active criterion of that story. The editor will not save an unanchored ATC, and the create and update database functions refuse an empty criteria list or any criterion outside the story. The story of an ATC cannot change after creation. Anchoring is what coverage and the traceability chain read.

UI labels: save hints "Pick a User Story to enable Save", "Bind at least one Acceptance Criterion to enable Save"; server messages "Bind to a user story before saving.", "Bind at least one acceptance criterion."

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Personal access tokenaccess_tokens, mintPat, token_prefix, scopes, runs.executor_token_id"Personal access tokens", "New token", "Revoke token"access_tokens (+ hash in access_token_secrets)supabase/migrations/0008_access_tokens.sql, lib/api/pat.ts, components/settings/IssueTokenModal.tsx

Business meaning: a long-lived credential that lets a CLI, CI job or AI agent call the API as its owner, limited by scopes and optionally bound to one workspace; it never exceeds the owner's own permissions, and the workspace:admin scope can only be granted on a workspace where the owner is admin or owner. Shown in full once at creation (bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>), never retrievable again. Issued and revoked from Settings in a browser session (or returned by the headless sign-in endpoints); a token cannot mint or revoke tokens. A token is also the executor's identity: a Run started or submitted with it records the token's name ("Agent — <token name>", fallback "API token"), and submitting a finished automated Run needs the run:execute scope on a token bound to a workspace. Revocation keeps the row for audit; leaving or deleting a workspace, or being removed from it, revokes the tokens bound to it.

UI labels: Settings > "Personal access tokens" ("Authenticate the Bunkai CLI and your CI against your account."), "Your tokens", "New token" / "Issue your first token", dialog "New personal access token" with "Token name" (placeholder "ci-deploy", "Lowercase and hyphens. Names the machine that will use it."), "Scopes", "Workspace — optional", "Expiry — optional" ("No expiry"); "Revoke token", toast "Token revoked"; run provenance "Agent — <token name>" / "CI — <name>".

Related terms: Workspace, Magic link, Run (a token caller may declare the agent or ci executor), Idempotency key. Values: token scope.

Abbreviations: PAT. Never bare "token" (also names magic-link and invite tokens).

Structure: business-data-context sections entity-access-token and state-access-token.

The first step (does this email have an account?) is rate-limited per network source; a new password must be 8 to 72 bytes (fewer characters when it holds accents or symbols); sign-up refuses reserved email domains that can never receive the code.

A module rename or description change is logged only when the value really changed. Business meaning: a client-chosen key that makes a repeated create request return the first result instead of creating a duplicate, kept per user and endpoint. It is required on ten endpoints: create a Test, start a Run, add Tests to a Test Plan, attach Test Plans to a Milestone, start a run-step image upload, start a bug evidence upload, start a billing checkout, save billing details, replace the payment method and retry a failed charge. It is optional on marking a run step. Reusing a key with a different body, or while the first request is still in flight, is refused. Two domain-level guards sit beside it: starting a Run with the same Test and start token within 24 hours returns the existing Run, and an automated Run submission may carry its own key in the body, unique per workspace for 24 hours (same key with a different payload is a conflict).

Related terms: Test, Run, Test Plan, Milestone, Evidence attachment, Billing checkout, Billing details. Values: idempotency status.

Archive and restore

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Archive (soft delete) and restorearchived_at, archived_by, archive_batch_id, bunkai_archive_atc, bunkai_restore_atc, bunkai_restore_module_subtree, bunkai_archive_milestone, bunkai_restore_milestone"Archive", "Archived", "Restore", "View archived", "Show archived rows", "Show archived"atcs, modules, user_stories, acceptance_criteria, milestonessupabase/migrations/0116_atc_archive_restore.sql, supabase/migrations/0117_module_restore.sql, supabase/migrations/0130_milestone_archive_restore.sql

Business meaning: Bunkai never hard-deletes authored work; it archives it. An archived item disappears from the lists people reuse (ATC pickers, library, workbench tree, Test builder) but stays as evidence: Runs, bugs, coverage and traceability keep reading what it produced. Archive works at three grains. A Module archive takes its whole subtree (sub-modules, stories, criteria, ATCs) and records exactly which rows it took, so restoring that Module brings back the same rows and nothing archived separately. A user story archive takes its criteria and ATCs with it. An ATC or a Milestone can be archived on its own. An archived item is read-only until it is restored; restoring an ATC whose parent is still archived hands it back to the parent, and it returns when the parent is restored. Archive and restore need the member role or higher and each real change writes one activity entry.

UI labels: ATC "Archive ATC" dialog ("Your unsaved edits to this ATC will be lost."), toast "Archived “<title>”. Restore it from the archived view in the ATC Library." with "View archived"; ATC Library archived view ("Nothing has been archived", "No ATC in this workspace has been archived on its own."), "Restore", "Retry restore"; archived ATC banner "This ATC is archived. It is read-only until it is restored.", "Archived with its <parent> … It comes back when that parent is restored."; Explorer "Show archived rows" / "Hide archived rows", "Restore module" dialog, toast "Restored “<name>” with …" or "Nothing else came back with it"; Milestones "Show archived" / "Hide archived", "Archive" / "Restore", banner "This milestone is archived. It is read-only until it is restored."

Related terms: Module, User story, ATC, Milestone, Coverage, Activity log. Not Workspace deletion (a separate, time-limited erase).

Abbreviations: none; the UI says "Archive" and the API route that archives a Module or a story is a DELETE.

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in

Business meaning: the unit of execution: a named, ordered chain of references to ATCs that walks one journey (an end-to-end or integration scenario). It holds references, not copies, so an ATC edit shows up in every Test that chains it; the same ATC may appear at several positions, so a chain position is addressed by its own chain-step id, not by the ATC. A Test belongs to the workspace, not to one project (its project is derived from the ATCs it chains), needs at least one ATC, a title of 1 to 200 characters, and can be reordered (same ATCs, new order) and tagged. Three reserved suite tags, smoke, sanity, regression, are lower-cased; custom tags keep their casing (at most 20, each up to 50 characters). A chained ATC that was later archived stays in the chain and is marked "Archived". Each Test carries an Automation status (manual-only by default) and, on its Run History, a flakiness signal. Tests have no delete.

UI labels: project section "Tests" (list columns "Name", "Chain", "Created"); "New Test", title placeholder "Name the journey this chain verifies", "Filter ATCs…", "A Test must include at least one ATC.", toast "Test created"; tabs "Steps" and "Run History"; "Chain order changed — unsaved.", toast "Chain reordered"; "Suites:" quick-add, toast "Tags updated."; chained ATC chip "Archived"; "Start run" with an "Environment…" picker, toast "Run started"; ATC side "Used by".

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Test Plantest_plans (status, verdict, summary, progress_snapshot), test_plan_tests, bunkai_plan_progress, bunkai_close_test_plan, bunkai_reopen_test_plan"Test Plans", "New plan", "Add tests", "Close plan", "Reopen"test_plans, test_plan_testssupabase/migrations/0073_test_plans.sql, supabase/migrations/0076_test_plan_tests.sql, supabase/migrations/0094_plan_progress.sql, supabase/migrations/0095_plan_close.sql, components/test-plans/

Business meaning: a curated group of Tests inside one project for a goal, cycle or release. It has a name (1 to 100 characters, unique per project ignoring case), a goal or release (up to 100) and a description (up to 500). A Test joins a plan at most once and may belong to several plans; only Tests whose whole chain lies in the plan's project can be added, and removing a Test from a plan only removes the membership. Progress is computed on view from each member Test's latest Run, whenever that Run happened: passed, failed, aborted, in progress (latest Run still running) or not run; the passed percentage is rounded down and reaches 100 only when every member passed. A plan is created Open and is editable only while Open. Closing it records a verdict (passed or failed, required) and an optional summary of up to 4000 characters, and freezes the progress as it stood; only the plan's creator (with write access) or an admin or owner can close or reopen it. Reopening returns it to Open and clears the verdict, summary and snapshot; the close and reopen history stays in the activity log. A plan can be attached to Milestones.

Business meaning: a named target date inside a project (for example a release cut) and the readiness of the Test Plans attached to it. The name is unique per project ignoring case (archived milestones included); the target date must be between today and five years ahead when it is set or changed, so a past milestone stays editable. Members and above attach up to 50 of the project's plans (all or nothing per selection) and detach them; a plan may serve several milestones and detaching never touches the plan. Readiness pools the tests of every attached plan (an open plan counts its live progress, a closed one its frozen progress) and is the passed share rounded down, 100 only when every pooled test passed; with no plans or no tests it reads "No readiness yet", never 0%. A milestone whose target date has passed and whose readiness is not 100 shows an "Overdue by N days" badge beside the date chip. A milestone can be archived (hidden, read-only, nothing deleted) and restored.

Run

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Run (test run, execution)runs, executor_mode, executor_name, executor_token_id, evidence_urls, start_token, abort_reason, bunkai_create_run, bunkai_submit_automated_run"Test Runs", "Start run", "Finish run", "Abort run", "Run History"runs (+ run_atcs, run_steps)supabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql, supabase/migrations/0121_automated_run_submission.sql, components/runs/RunnerView.tsx

Business meaning: one execution of a Test against a project environment, by a human, an agent or CI. At start it freezes a copy of the Test's chain (every ATC position and every step), so later ATC edits never change the evidence. The executor marks each run step, then closes the Run with a verdict they choose (passed or failed), or aborts it with a reason. Only a running Run accepts marks; a closed Run is final. An automated executor can instead submit a Run that is already finished, in one call, with a result for every chain position, an overall verdict that must agree with them (passed with no failed step, failed with at least one), a duration and up to 20 evidence links; it is recorded as executor agent with the token's name. A Run with no step activity is closed automatically as aborted: after 60 minutes for agent and CI Runs, after 4 hours otherwise ("Auto-closed by inactivity sweep"). Each Run counts as Manual or Automated execution mode. The starter is notified when it finishes or aborts, unless they closed it themselves in the browser. Every Run of the workspace is listed in the Test Runs index, and a closed Run can be compared with the previous one. Runs have no delete.

UI labels: sidebar "Test Runs" opens the workspace index (filters "Project" / "All projects", "Outcome", "Environment" / "All environments", "Mode"; "Load older runs"); project section "Test Runs" (run report with filters, "All modules", "Mode"); "Start run", toast "Run started"; runner "Finish run", "Abort run" with "Abort reason" (placeholder "Why are you aborting this run?"), toasts "Run finished", "Run aborted"; status labels "Running", "Passed", "Failed", "Aborted"; executor labels "Human", "Agent", "CI" (the Home active-runs panel says "Manual" for human); provenance "Agent — <token name>", "CI — <name>"; "Compare".

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Run step (step result) and run ATC (position result)run_steps (status, note, evidence_url), run_atcs (source_atc_id), bunkai_mark_run_step"Pass" / "Fail" / "Block", "Step marked", "Unrun"run_steps, run_atcssupabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql, supabase/migrations/0042_run_step_mark.sql, supabase/migrations/0122_streamed_run_step_results.sql, lib/runs/mark-step-view.ts

Business meaning: the frozen copy of one ATC step inside a Run, and the verdict recorded on it: passed, failed or blocked, with an optional note, an evidence link and up to 10 screenshot attachments. In the browser a marked step can be re-marked while the Run is running (last mark wins, no history). An API client that streams results gets a stricter rule: reporting the same result again is a harmless repeat, reporting a different one is refused as a conflict. Each chain position (run ATC) carries its own verdict derived from its steps and remembers which ATC it came from, so Runs can be compared; this per-ATC result is what coverage and traceability read as an ATC's real execution status. When the Run is closed, every step still pending becomes skipped. A failed step is where a bug is filed from.

Grain: the product glossary separates three run vocabularies: the Run (running / passed / failed / aborted), the position and step (pending / passed / failed / blocked / skipped), and the traceability chip that combines both. aborted exists only at the Run grain (.context/business/domain-glossary.md §3).

Business meaning: an uploaded screenshot (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MiB each) kept as proof, next to the older evidence links. On a run step: up to 10 per step, 50 MiB per step and 250 MiB per Run; members, admins and owners attach while the Run is running, only the uploader removes their own, and once the Run closes the evidence is read-only forever. On a bug: images are uploaded while filing and claimed by the bug when it is filed; links plus images count together against the bug's 10-item and 50 MiB limit, the set is frozen at filing, and an upload never filed expires after 3 hours. Files are private: only members of the workspace can view them, through Bunkai, never by a public link.

Flakiness

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Flakiness signal (per Test)bunkai_list_test_runs.flakiness (sample, flips, aborted_skipped), FlakinessBand"Stable", "Occasionally flaky", "Flaky" (Run History)computed (no table)supabase/migrations/0099_run_history_flakiness.sql, lib/runs/flakiness.ts

Business meaning: how often a Test's verdict flips between passed and failed across its 10 most recent passed or failed Runs, shown on its Run History. A flip is two consecutive Runs with different verdicts; aborted Runs are skipped, not counted as a break. With fewer than 5 verdict Runs the Test is not judged and the screen says how many more Runs are needed. With no flips it is Stable; flips on at most one third of the consecutive pairs make it Occasionally flaky; more is Flaky. It is computed on read from Run history; nothing is stored and it is not per environment.

UI labels: headline such as "Flaky — 5 flips in the last 10 runs (56%)" or "Stable — no flips in the last N runs"; "Not enough runs yet — N of 5 needed (… more Runs needed)".

Related terms: Test, Run, Run comparison. Values: flakiness band.

Business meaning: a defect tracked natively inside Bunkai. It always belongs to a project and a module, and is either filed from a failed run step (the run, step and ATC are linked automatically as its origin) or filed manually with no origin. It has a title (5 to 200 characters), a severity, an optional description and steps to reproduce, up to 10 evidence items (links plus uploaded screenshots, 50 MiB in all, frozen at filing), a reporter and an optional assignee, who must be an active member above viewer. A member who can write may correct its title, severity, description and steps to reproduce; status, assignee, origin and evidence are not touched, and a correction based on an outdated copy is refused so nobody overwrites a newer one. Its status moves one stage forward at a time and never back. Removing a member unassigns their bugs. A project can queue its bugs for Jira through defect sync, but nothing sends them yet. Bugs have no delete and stay readable after their module is archived (tagged "Archived"); defects whose own module is archived are left out of the lists.

Severity: stored as P1 to P4, rendered as words: P1 Critical, P2 Major, P3 Minor, P4 Trivial (lib/bugs/constants.ts). Not the same scale as ATC Priority.

UI labels: sidebar "Bug Reports" opens the workspace defect index (most severe first; filters "Project" / "All projects", "Status", "Severity"; columns "Defect", "Title", "Severity", "Status", "Module", "Origin", "Assignee"; "Load more defects"); project section "Bug Reports" with List and Heatmap views; "New bug" / "Report bug" dialog ("What went wrong?", "Select a module…", "Evidence", "File bug"), toast "Bug filed"; detail "Origin", "Details", "Evidence", "Steps to reproduce", "Filed manually. This defect was reported directly — no test run or ATC is linked.", "Unassigned", "Edit" (correction dialog: "One step per line. Evidence, status and assignee are not changed here.", "Current version", "Defect updated.", "Nothing changed, so nothing was saved.", "This defect changed since you opened it…"); one forward action per status: "Start progress", "Mark resolved", "Close"; toast "Bug status updated".

Related terms: Run step, Module, ATC, Evidence attachment, Defect sync, Defect heatmap, Notification, Traceability chain. Values: bug severity, bug status, bug sync state.

Abbreviations: the product glossary distinguishes Defect (any deviation) from Bug (found during execution); the UI uses "Bug" in navigation and "Defect" in the workspace index, the correction dialog and the traceability view.

Coverage

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Coverage (per criterion, per module, per workspace)bunkai_report_project_coverage, bunkai_report_workspace_coverage, states uncovered / not_run / executed; module no_acs / uncovered / not_run / fully_covered"Coverage by module", "Coverage gaps", "Never run"computed (no table)supabase/migrations/0090_project_coverage_skipped_blocked_not_run.sql, supabase/migrations/0116_atc_archive_restore.sql, components/coverage/ProjectCoverageView.tsx

Business meaning: how much of a project's acceptance criteria is backed by tests that actually ran. Per criterion: uncovered when no ATC of the project is bound to it (an authoring gap); not run when a bound ATC's most recent result is anything but passed or failed, including never run, skipped and blocked (an execution gap); otherwise executed. When an ATC appears several times in its latest Run, it counts as executed if any of those occurrences passed or failed. An ATC archived on its own still counts for what it already ran, so its criterion is never "uncovered" because of the archive; one that never ran no longer holds the criterion at not run, unless every bound ATC is archived and unrun. ATCs under an archived module are excluded. A failed ATC still counts as coverage: coverage and health are separate axes. A module rolls up as no criteria, uncovered, not run or fully covered. The two gaps have different owners and must never be merged into one "not covered" state. Shown on the project Metrics page and summarised on Home; the workspace figure is computed for all projects in one pass and equals the sum of the project figures.

UI labels: "Coverage by module", "Executed vs. bound-but-never-run vs. unbound acceptance criteria", "Coverage gaps", "No coverage gaps.", "Zero linked ATCs: nothing bound at all", "Never run" (Home says "awaiting execution" for the same state; the product glossary records this drift).

Related terms: Acceptance criterion, Anchoring, Run step, Module, Archive and restore, Traceability chain. Values: coverage state, module coverage status.

Business meaning: bugs per active module over a rolling window of 7, 30 or 90 days, with a week-over-week trend. It now updates itself while open: when a bug is filed in the project the heatmap re-reads the report within seconds, without a reload. It is the second view of the Bug Reports screen and the reason modules are first-class.

Business meaning: a message to one member about an event that concerns them. Run and bug notifications are produced automatically from the activity log: the run starter when their Run finishes or aborts (not when they closed it themselves in the browser); the new assignee when a bug is assigned or reassigned; the reporter and assignee when a bug's status changes, never the person who changed it. A mention in Team chat notifies the mentioned member. Each recipient gets at most one per event. The recipient's preferences are applied when the event happens: with In-app off the item never appears in the inbox, the bell or live updates, but is still sent once in the next email digest when Email is on; with both off nothing is delivered. Changing a preference later never hides or revives existing items. Mentions always reach the inbox. The inbox shows the last 90 days, updates live, and keeps an item readable as "This item is no longer available." when its entity is gone or hidden. Items are unread until read one by one or all at once.

UI labels: "Notifications" panel (bell "Notifications, N unread" / "Notifications, all read"), "Mark all as read", empty state "No notifications yet", fallback "This item is no longer available."

Related terms: Activity log, Notification preference, Email digest, Run, Bug, Mention. Values: notification event type.

Business meaning: an owner's request to erase a workspace. Owner only, from a browser session; other members cannot veto. From that moment the workspace is invisible to everyone, its tokens and pending invites are revoked, and the owner and every active member get an email with a restore link. Anyone working in it when it disappears is moved to another workspace with a notice (or to onboarding when none is left). For 30 days the owner can restore it (data intact, revoked tokens and invites stay revoked); the moment 30 days have passed, restore is refused even if the daily purge has not run yet, and the purge then deletes it permanently. A tombstone record (name, slug, requester, member count, row counts) survives the purge for audit. A request that fails halfway leaves the workspace untouched.

Business meaning: the subscription tier of a workspace, which sets its limits and price. Community: free, 5 seats, 3 projects, 30-day retention. Cloud: 24.00 USD per seat, 25 seats, 50 projects, 90-day retention. Enterprise: custom price, no limits. A seat is one active member counted against the tier. The limits that apply are those of the effective plan: the stored plan, except that a Cloud workspace whose grace period after a failed renewal has ended is treated as Community until the charge succeeds. Only the project limit is enforced (project creation is refused above it, with a warning banner before); seats and retention are shown as usage meters and never block. Admins and owners see the billing overview, billing details and invoices; only the owner can upgrade (see Billing checkout), edit details, replace the card or retry a charge. There is no downgrade or cancellation path.

UI labels: Settings > "Billing" ("Plan, seats, and usage for this workspace."), "Current plan", "Seats", "Usage", "Run history" (retention meter), "Upgrade plan", "Unable to load billing info"; Community shows "No active subscription"; "Approaching plan limit" banner and the plan-limit dialog.

InvoiceInvoice (status paid / issued / failed), listWorkspaceInvoices"Invoices", "Download", "Paid", "Issued", "Failed"none in Bunkai (read from Stripe)lib/billing/invoices.ts, components/billing/InvoiceHistoryCard.tsx

Business meaning: a bill Stripe issued for the workspace's Cloud subscription, listed newest first with its number, billed period, seats, amount and status, and downloadable as PDF. Stripe is the source of truth: Bunkai stores no copy and only lists invoices that were actually issued (no drafts, no voided ones). Only the owner and admins of a paid workspace see the list.

UI labels: "Invoices" ("No invoices yet", "Loading invoices", "Load more"), columns invoice number ("No number yet"), period ("From … UTC"), seats, "Amount", status chips "Paid" / "Issued" / "Failed", "Download" ("PDF not available").

Related terms: Billing details, Billing Plan, Grace period. Values: invoice display status.

Structure: business-data-context section integration-stripe.

Grace period

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Failed renewal and grace periodworkspace_grace_periods (ends_at), workspace_billing_state.payment_state, bunkai_effective_plan"Renewal charge failed", "Retry charge", "Replace payment method"workspace_grace_periods, workspace_billing_statesupabase/migrations/0113_billing_details_invoices.sql, components/billing/FailedRenewalBanner.tsx

Business meaning: what happens when a Cloud renewal charge fails. The first failed renewal opens a 14-day window (in UTC); Stripe's own automatic retries never extend it. During the window the workspace keeps its paid limits; from the exact moment it ends, every limit is read as Community, although the stored plan stays Cloud and nothing is deleted. The owner can replace the card and retry the charge at any time; only Stripe's confirmation that the invoice was paid marks the workspace recovered and restores its limits.

UI labels: banner "Renewal charge failed" with "Your workspace keeps its paid limits until <date> UTC." or, after the window, "Your grace period ended on <date> UTC. This workspace is on Community limits and nothing was deleted. Replace the payment method and retry the charge to restore your plan."; buttons "Retry charge", "Replace payment method".

Related terms: Billing Plan, Invoice, Billing details, Project (the project limit follows the effective plan). Values: payment state.

Structure: business-data-context section flow-billing-upgrade (not yet refreshed; the payment state machine has four states and needs a data-map state section, see discovery gaps).

Business meaning: the keyboard overlay (Cmd/Ctrl+K) that searches the active workspace and jumps to a result. It returns ATCs, Tests, Projects, Modules, Bugs and Runs in that fixed group order, only what the caller can see. It is an overlay, not a screen. The product glossary asks to say "command palette", not "search bar" (the ATC library's in-page filter).

UI labels: "Command palette", "Search…", groups "ATCs", "Tests", "Projects", "Modules", "Bugs", "Runs", error "Search failed. Try again.", "Esc".

Related terms: ATC, Test, Project, Module, Bug, Run.

Structure: business-data-context section flow-reports.

Discovery gaps

The following items could not be verified from code, or code and docs disagree, and require human confirmation:

  • Docs ahead of code (narrowed). Since 98ee1b4 the code delivered Channel (one #general per workspace), Message, Mention, Rich Link, Execution Mode, Automation Status (column only), Invoice and the subscription renewal and grace cycle, so those now have term- sections. Still missing from code: per-project channels, a writer for Automation Status, a CI Results File upload, and the sending half of the one-way bug sync to Jira (the queue fills, nothing drains it). Whether they are still planned is a product question.
  • Product glossary behind code. .context/business/domain-glossary.md still says Milestone readiness "is not built yet" and lists "Overdue" on a Milestone as a banned label, while the code now computes readiness and shows "Overdue by N days" when the target date passed and readiness is below 100 (lib/milestones/readiness-view.ts, supabase/migrations/0112_milestone_plans.sql). Which source is authoritative is unruled.
  • Mentions preference contradicts shipped chat. The Mentions row of Settings > Notifications is still locked with "these controls unlock when it ships", but Team chat and mentions shipped and mentions are delivered in-app with no preference gate (components/settings/NotificationPreferencesGrid.tsx, supabase/migrations/0123_chat_mentions.sql). Whether Email for mentions or an unlock is planned is unconfirmed.
  • Glossary vs code on environments. The product glossary says Staging and Production are seeded per project; the code seeded them only once, for projects that existed when runs shipped (supabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql), and new projects start with none, so they cannot run a Test until someone adds an environment. Intended behaviour unconfirmed.
  • Dead execution status on ATCs. atcs.status is displayed (status dot, sidebar filter "fail / blocked / unrun") but never written, so it always reads unrun even after Runs, while chat rich links already show the real latest result. Whether it should mirror the latest run result is unconfirmed.
  • Assertions are not part of a Run. Runs snapshot ATC steps only; assertions are neither copied, shown in the runner, nor part of an automated submission, although the editor describes them as "checked by every executor". How an executor is meant to apply them is unconfirmed.
  • Limits shown but not enforced. Seat and retention limits appear as usage meters; invites and acceptance do not check seats and nothing deletes old runs. Only the project limit blocks (now grace-aware). Whether enforcement is planned is a product question.
  • Billing lifecycle (narrowed). Upgrade, renewal invoices, failed-renewal grace, card replacement and charge retry exist. No downgrade or cancellation; Enterprise has no path that sets it. Revenue figures beyond the per-seat price are not in code.
  • Unreachable values. Member status invited and suspended, chat channel kinds other than general, and Automation status candidate / automated have no path that sets them; their meaning is inferred from names and docs. (Test plan closed is now reachable.)
  • No story-level restore. Archiving a user story takes its criteria and ATCs, but only a Module restore brings a story back; there is no restore for a story archived on its own (supabase/migrations/0111_user_story_archive_cascade.sql, supabase/migrations/0117_module_restore.sql). Intended behaviour unconfirmed.
  • Label drift (unruled). Executor human renders "Human" in run lists and comparison, "Manual" on Home and in the new Mode filter and bug origin; a bound-but-never-run criterion renders "Never run" on Metrics and "awaiting execution" on Home; run verdicts render "Passed" / "Pass"; the same item is "Bug" in navigation and "Defect" in the workspace index and correction dialog. Recorded as unruled in the product glossary §5. (The global sidebar entries now all link.)
  • Unused schema. feature_flags still has no reader or writer in app code. (user_view_state is now used by saved views.)
  • Data map behind this map. business-data-context (last updated 2026-10-12) has no section for Team chat, saved views (its entities row describes the pre-0093 shape), evidence attachments, the Jira connection (its integration-jira still describes platform credentials), defect sync state, milestone plans, archive batches, billing state and grace periods. The billing payment state has four values and needs a state section there. Several new term- sections point to the nearest existing section until it is refreshed.
  • Revenue Streams and Cost Structure beyond the Cloud price rest on the business doc only (Low confidence).
  • No i18n bundle. UI labels come from component JSX; the QA guide page (app/qa/) is in Spanish while the app UI is in English. Confirm the product's official UI language.
  • Diagrams. No figure drawn: this map is tables by design (figures are optional here); a relationship overview can be added later after the diagrams capability check.
